title: Azure Policy and tags: enforce standards, audit compliance, govern metadata
learningObjective: Assign built-in policies at the right scope, predict the effect on new requests and existing resources, use exclusions, exemptions and enforcement mode, and apply and govern tags at scale.
foundation: Azure Policy is a set of rules about what your resources may look like: which regions are allowed, which VM sizes, which tags must be present.

A policy definition describes the rule and what to do when it is broken (its effect). An assignment applies that definition to a scope, such as a management group, subscription or resource group, and everything under it inherits it.
The common effects are Deny (block the request), Audit (allow it but flag it as non-compliant) and Modify (fix the request, for example by adding a missing tag).
Policy does not delete or change resources that already exist when you assign it. It marks them non-compliant so you can see them, and some effects can fix them later through a remediation task.

Tags are name/value labels such as costCenter=CC-100 or environment=prod. They help you group costs, automate and find resources. Tags are not inherited automatically; Azure Policy is how you require or copy them.
engineer: Building blocks: a definition (JSON policyRule with if/then and parameters), an initiative (policy set) that groups definitions, an assignment (definition or initiative + scope + parameters + notScopes + enforcementMode), and an exemption (assignment + scope + category Waiver or Mitigated, with an optional expiry).

Effect evaluation order for a create/update request: Disabled is checked first, then Append and Modify (which can change the request), then Deny, then Audit. After the resource provider succeeds, AuditIfNotExists and DeployIfNotExists evaluate related resources. Because Modify runs before Deny, 'inherit tag from resource group' can satisfy 'require tag' in the same request.

Effects: Append, Audit, AuditIfNotExists, Deny, DenyAction, DeployIfNotExists, Disabled, Manual and Modify. Many built-in definitions expose the effect as a parameter so one definition can audit in dev and deny in prod.

enforcementMode DoNotEnforce (portal: Policy enforcement Disabled) stops the effect from being applied, so there are no denies and no modifications, but compliance is still evaluated and reported. Use it to test the impact of a new Deny before you enforce it.

Existing resources are evaluated in compliance scans. A scan starts shortly after a new assignment takes effect, runs every 24 hours, and can be triggered on demand (az policy state trigger-scan). Modify and DeployIfNotExists can fix existing resources only through a remediation task, which uses the assignment's managed identity. That identity needs the roles listed in the definition's roleDefinitionIds.

Policy applies to Resource Manager (control-plane) requests. Delete requests are not evaluated by Deny; the DenyAction effect exists for blocking delete actions. Resource actions such as start/stop (POST) are not evaluated by Deny.

Tags: up to 50 tag name/value pairs per resource, resource group and subscription. Tag names are limited to 512 characters (128 for storage accounts) and values to 256. Not every resource type supports tags. Tags on a resource group are not inherited by its resources. Tag values are stored as plain text, so never put secrets in them. The Tag Contributor role lets someone manage tags without access to the resources themselves.

Assigning policy requires Microsoft.Authorization/policyAssignments/write, which Owner and Resource Policy Contributor have. Contributor does not, because Microsoft.Authorization writes are in its NotActions.

animation.caption: Send create/update requests through Azure Policy effects, try exclusions and enforcement mode, then scan existing resources.

example.title: Location, tag and cost governance for a new subscription
body: Contoso assigns 'Allowed locations' (West Europe, North Europe) at the Contoso management group so every subscription inherits it. A data-residency exception for one sandbox RG is handled with an exemption (Waiver, expiring in 90 days) rather than by removing the assignment.

Finance needs costCenter on every resource. The platform team assigns 'Require a tag on resource groups' (so every RG carries costCenter) and 'Inherit a tag from the resource group if missing' (Modify) with a system-assigned managed identity. New resources pick up the RG's value automatically; a remediation task back-fills existing resources.
Before switching a new Deny on in production they assign it with DoNotEnforce for a week and review the compliance report, so they know which pipelines would break.

prerequisites: Target scope ID (management group, subscription or resource group)
For Modify/DeployIfNotExists: a managed identity on the assignment and a location for it
permissions: Tag changes: write on the resource, or Tag Contributor
limits: Up to 200 policy or initiative assignments per scope
50 tags per resource, resource group or subscription; tag name 512 chars (128 for storage accounts), value 256 chars
Tags are not inherited by default
portal: Policy > Definitions: filter by category, open a built-in such as 'Allowed locations' and review its JSON and parameters.
Assign policy: choose Scope (and Exclusions), set Parameters, set Policy enforcement (Enabled/Disabled), and on the Remediation tab create a managed identity for Modify/DeployIfNotExists.
Policy > Compliance: drill into an assignment to see non-compliant resources and the reason for each.
Policy > Remediation: create a remediation task for non-compliant resources under a Modify or DeployIfNotExists assignment.
Policy > Exemptions: create a Waiver or Mitigated exemption for a scope, optionally with an expiration date.
Any resource or resource group > Tags: add, edit or delete tags. Resource groups > Edit columns > Tags to view them at scale.
configuration.cli:
# Find the built-in definition by display name instead of hard-coding its ID
defId=$(az policy definition list --query "[?displayName=='Allowed locations'].name" -o tsv)
az policy assignment create --name allowed-locations --scope /subscriptions/<sub-id> \
  --policy "$defId" --params '{"listOfAllowedLocations":{"value":["westeurope","northeurope"]}}' \
  --not-scopes /subscriptions/<sub-id>/resourceGroups/rg-sandbox
az policy assignment update --name allowed-locations --scope /subscriptions/<sub-id> --enforcement-mode DoNotEnforce
az policy state trigger-scan --resource-group rg-prod
az policy state summarize --resource-group rg-prod
az policy remediation create --name backfill-costcenter --policy-assignment inherit-costcenter --resource-group rg-prod
# Tags
az tag update --resource-id <resource-id> --operation Merge --tags costCenter=CC-100 environment=prod
az resource list --tag costCenter=CC-100 -o table
configuration.powershell:
$def = Get-AzPolicyDefinition -Builtin | Where-Object DisplayName -eq 'Allowed locations'
New-AzPolicyAssignment -Name 'allowed-locations' -Scope '/subscriptions/<sub-id>' -PolicyDefinition $def `
  -PolicyParameterObject @{ listOfAllowedLocations = @('westeurope','northeurope') } `
  -NotScope '/subscriptions/<sub-id>/resourceGroups/rg-sandbox'
Start-AzPolicyComplianceScan -ResourceGroupName rg-prod
Get-AzPolicyState -ResourceGroupName rg-prod -Filter "ComplianceState eq 'NonCompliant'"
# Tags
Update-AzTag -ResourceId <resource-id> -Tag @{ costCenter = 'CC-100' } -Operation Merge
Get-AzResource -TagName costCenter -TagValue CC-100

lab.objective: Predict and prove how Deny, Modify, Audit, exclusions and DoNotEnforce affect new and existing resources.
steps: Assign 'Allowed locations' at the management group. Create VM vm2 in eastus and watch Policy deny it.
Assign again with 'Exclude rg-sandbox', then create the eastus VM in rg-sandbox. The request succeeds because of the exclusion.

Use the scenario 'Require + inherit costCenter tag'. Create a VM in rg-prod without tags: Modify adds costCenter=CC-100 before Deny is evaluated, so the request succeeds. Repeat in rg-sandbox, which has no tag to inherit: Deny fires.
Run a compliance scan. Existing st1 (eastus, no tags) is reported non-compliant but is not deleted or changed.
Change an assignment to DoNotEnforce and resend a non-compliant request. It succeeds, but the outcome says it would be non-compliant.
expected: RequestDisallowedByPolicy for eastus in an in-scope RG.
Final tags on the vm2 request include costCenter from rg-prod.
The compliance scan lists non-compliant existing resources without modifying them.

troubleshooting.cause: A Deny assignment at this scope or a parent matched the request.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the error's policyAssignmentId/policyDefinitionId, then fix the template, or request an exemption if the exception is justified.

troubleshooting.symptom: A new policy shows 'Not started' or no results.
troubleshooting.cause: The compliance evaluation has not run yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait for the evaluation cycle or run az policy state trigger-scan / Start-AzPolicyComplianceScan.

troubleshooting.symptom: Non-compliant resources stay non-compliant under a Modify policy.
troubleshooting.cause: Modify only alters new create/update requests; existing resources need a remediation task.
troubleshooting.fix: Create a remediation task, and make sure the assignment's managed identity has the required roles.

troubleshooting.cause: policyAssignments/write is excluded by Contributor's NotActions.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Resource Policy Contributor or Owner at that scope.

troubleshooting.symptom: Resources in a tagged resource group show no tags in cost analysis.
troubleshooting.cause: Resource group tags are not inherited by resources.
troubleshooting.fix: Use an 'Inherit a tag from the resource group' Modify policy plus remediation, or enable tag inheritance in Cost Management.

comparisons.difference: RBAC decides who may perform an operation; Policy decides whether the resulting resource configuration is allowed. A request needs both.
Locks stop delete/modify operations on specific scopes for everyone; Policy evaluates the properties of what is being created or updated.

comparisons.service: AWS Organizations SCPs and AWS Config rules
comparisons.difference: SCPs limit which API actions accounts can call; Config rules evaluate resource compliance. Azure Policy combines preventive (Deny) and detective (Audit) controls in one service.

misconceptions.myth: Assigning a Deny policy deletes existing non-compliant resources.
misconceptions.reality: Existing resources are only reported as non-compliant; nothing is deleted.

misconceptions.myth: Tags on a resource group apply to the resources inside it.
misconceptions.reality: Tags are not inherited; use Policy (Modify) to copy them.
It stops enforcement but still evaluates and reports compliance.

misconceptions.myth: An exclusion and an exemption are the same thing.
misconceptions.reality: Exclusions (notScopes) are set on the assignment; exemptions are separate resources with a category, an optional expiry and their own audit trail.

architectureDecisions: Assign guardrails at management groups so new subscriptions are governed from day one.
Group related definitions into initiatives (for example a tagging initiative) to manage them as one assignment.
Prefer exemptions with expiry dates over permanent exclusions for one-off exceptions.
Roll out new Deny assignments with DoNotEnforce first, and review compliance before enforcing.

walkthrough.subtitle: Make rules that Azure enforces for you, and label resources so you can find and charge them.

steps.label: Wild west
steps.title: Resources appear everywhere, unlabelled
body: People create VMs in random regions, with no labels. Nobody knows who owns what, and the bill is a mystery.

steps.label: Policy vs RBAC
steps.title: Two different questions
body: RBAC asks: is this person allowed to act? Azure Policy asks: is this resource, as configured, allowed to exist?
A Contributor may create a VM (RBAC), but policy can still block it because it is in the wrong region.

steps.label: Building blocks
steps.title: Definition, initiative, assignment
body: A policy definition is one rule, such as 'Allowed locations'. An initiative groups several definitions. An assignment applies a definition or initiative at a scope (management group, subscription or resource group), with parameters such as the list of regions.
You can exclude child scopes from an assignment.

steps.label: Effects
steps.title: What happens when a rule is broken
body: Deny blocks the request. Audit allows it but marks it non-compliant. Modify and Append change the request, for example adding a tag. DeployIfNotExists deploys something missing, such as a diagnostic setting.
Existing resources are evaluated too and shown in the compliance view; fixing them needs a remediation task.

callout.text: Deny stops new requests; it does not delete resources that already exist.

steps.label: Tags
steps.title: Tags: labels for finding and charging
body: A tag is a name-value pair such as env = prod. Use tags to filter cost reports and find owners. Resources do not inherit tags from their resource group automatically.
Use the built-in policy 'Inherit a tag from the resource group if missing' (Modify effect) to copy them down.

callout.text: Up to 50 tags per resource. Not every resource type supports tags.

steps.label: Recap
steps.title: Policy and tags
body: RBAC controls people; policy controls resources; tags label them.
recap: RBAC = may you act? Policy = is the resource allowed?
Definition > initiative > assignment at a scope
Tags are not inherited by default
Use a Modify policy to inherit tags

handsOn.title: Block a region with policy and copy tags from the resource group
handsOn.cost: Free. Azure Policy and tags cost nothing; the storage account you try to create is blocked.
before: Signed in at portal.azure.com as Owner of a subscription (a free or pay-as-you-go account works). Work in a resource group called rg-az104-lab.
If rg-az104-lab does not exist yet: search 'Resource groups' > Create > name rg-az104-lab, region UAE North (or any region near you) > Review + create > Create.

steps.do: Open rg-az104-lab > Tags. Add env = lab and owner = your name. Apply.
steps.see: The two tags on the resource group's Overview.

steps.do: Search 'Policy' > Assignments > Assign policy. Scope: your subscription and resource group rg-az104-lab. Policy definition: search 'Allowed locations' and select it.
steps.see: The Basics tab with your scope and the policy name.

steps.do: Parameters tab: Allowed locations = UAE North only. Review + create > Create.
steps.see: A new assignment listed. Wait about 5–10 minutes for it to take effect.

steps.do: Try to create a storage account in rg-az104-lab with region East US.
steps.see: Validation fails: 'Resource was disallowed by policy', naming the Allowed locations assignment.

steps.do: Policy > Assignments > Assign policy again, same scope. Definition: 'Inherit a tag from the resource group if missing'. Parameter tag name: env. On the Remediation tab tick 'Create a remediation task'. Create.
steps.see: A second assignment. Policies that change resources need a managed identity, which the wizard creates.

steps.do: Create a small storage account in rg-az104-lab in your allowed region (Standard, LRS). Do not add tags yourself.
steps.see: Once deployed, its Tags page shows env = lab, copied from the resource group.
Your assignments with a compliance state. New results can take up to 30 minutes.

check: Creating in East US was denied.
The new storage account has the env tag without you adding it.
cleanup: Policy > Assignments: delete both lab assignments.
When you finish for the day: Resource groups > rg-az104-lab > Delete resource group > type the name > Delete. This removes everything inside it.
